highlights.title: The RealReal won’t let AI agents hog designer clothing
highlights.summary: The RealReal, a secondhand luxury fashion consignment retailer, said it's updating its bot defense system, effectively making it harder for AI agents to shop on its site.
body: Previous reporting by The Verge found that Meta’s Muse could be used to effectively block other shoppers from purchasing items for hours.

The change comes days after The Verge reported that an AI agent could be used to take advantage of The RealReal’s item reserve system. On the retailer’s website, an item goes “on hold” and is unavailable for other customers to buy for 20 minutes once it’s placed in a user’s shopping cart. Using Meta’s Muse, The Verge was able to instruct the AI agent to continuously re-add The RealReal listings in a shopping cart as soon as the 20-minute hold had expired, effectively blocking other shoppers from purchasing products for hours or longer.

After publication, chief technology officer Luke Friang said in an email that the company had addressed the Muse use case flagged by The Verge ’s story. The RealReal’s bot defense configuration now makes it much more difficult for all agents to log in, add items to cart, and check out, Friang said. Agents will still be able to surface listings from The RealReal and direct Muse users to product pages, Friang said, adding that the company will continue to strengthen protections as AI-powered online shopping evolves.

highlights.title: The Anthropic S-1 Filing Is Also an AI Doomsday Primer
highlights.summary: Anthropic thinks “closing the loop” is the best path to AI triumph—and a recipe for “existential” threats to humanity.
body: Anthropic has officially filed the prospectus for its initial public offering, which means the AI lab has put all kinds of formerly private information on display. While the prospectus contains the eye-popping revenue—and even larger expenditures—you might expect, the biggest section of the filing by far is given over to “risk factors,” which are all the things that could squash Anthropic’s big plans. Or, in this case, humanity itself.

While much has been made about the extent to which AI represents an existential threat to humankind, the specific mechanisms by which it could bring about that destruction are largely opaque. If nothing else, the 94 pages that Anthropic’s prospectus devotes to risk factors make clear both where it sees the danger coming from, and the ways in which its researchers are running toward it in order to win the AI arms race.
Anthropic is careful to tie that outcome, though, to a specific process: recursive self-improvement.

highlights.title: Fearnley retires injured to give Fery victory at Vienna Open
highlights.summary: Jacob Fearnley retired with an injury after losing 5-1 in the first set against Arthur Fery to give his fellow countryman a place in the second round at the Vienna Open.
body: Fearnley was broken by Fery in just his second service game, with the British No 1 winning the next two games on the bounce and looking set to consign his opponent to a comprehensive first-set loss.
Fearnley, though, then put a stop to the contest, shaking the umpire's hand and retiring with an unspecified injury, allowing Fery safe passage to the next stage of the competition.
Fery will face the winner of No 6 seed Francis Tiafoe and Lorenzo Musetti - the latter of whom he lost against in straight sets at the US Open - in the second round.

body: In episode 4 of VisionQuest, Vision (Paul Bettany) and the other AIs housed in his mind determine that the Butcherbird’s next victim will be Katerina Wells (Mary McDonnell), the last surviving board member of Markridge Biotech. To stop the killer, Vision, Tommy (Ruaridh Mollica), and Lisa Molinari (Lauren Morais) infiltrate a gala Wells will be speaking at, though their rescue does not go as planned.

At the party, the Butcherbird Killer is revealed to be Jocasta, an AI based upon Josephine Carrington, a Markridge Biotech board member who died in 2008 due to illness, though not before uploading her consciousness into the Jocasta AI. Carrington/Jocasta is enraged that her fellow board members sold off her company to Stark, and it seems that she is now getting her revenge as Jocasta. On top of that, she seems to be collecting biokeys from her victims for some yet-to-be-revealed larger plan.

highlights.title: ‘Minimum Wage’ Review: Netflix’s Format-Breaking Hangout Series Makes Good on the Promise of Short Episode Running Times
highlights.summary: 'Fresh Off the Boat' star Randall Park is the biggest name in this adaptation of the web series of the same name from production company American High.
body: There were plenty of reasons why Quibi, the short-form streaming platform, failed within eight months of its 2020 launch.

I made fun of Quibi and I’ll continue to, but one thing I won’t deny: The executives behind Quibi were probably right that shorter episodes were a key element of the future of storytelling, if not the entirety of the future.

Two weeks ago, Freeform released Coven Academy, a supernatural YA drama that aired on television with standard episodic lengths but then streamed with episodes running between 12 and 23 minutes. I won’t tell you that Coven Academy is a good show, but thanks to the length of episodes it moves along like gangbusters, especially at a time when power players like HBO and Netflix still insist that hour-long dramas should be closer to 65 or 70 minutes per episode if they’re “prestigious.”
Enter Minimum Wage, a streaming version of the web series of the same name from the production company American High.

body: Apple says a ‘small number’ of iPhone Duos have shown the cracked inner screen problem and that owners should contact AppleCare.

Shortly after launch, iPhone Duo users started reporting similar issues where the hinge would tighten, and opening the device caused a crack and the distinctive bright lines on the display. One user in Australia said that an Apple Store replaced their unit “on the spot.”

This weekend, iFixit published its teardown of the phone and gave its perspective on why some phones might be cracking. Where the damage has been happening, iFixit shows how the foldable screen might be pushing against a center bar.

The Verge has contacted Apple about the reports, but has not received an on-the-record response about the issues with these new phones. They’re some of the first devices to launch after new CEO John Ternus took over from Tim Cook.

highlights.title: Celtic & Rangers wait for stadium closures ruling
highlights.summary: Rangers and Celtic submit appeals against a ruling that they must play their next home Scottish Cup ties behind closed doors following scenes of disorder in last season's competition.
body: Rangers and Celtic are waiting for a Scottish FA appellate tribunal to rule on their respective appeals against an order that they must play their next home Scottish Cup ties behind closed doors.
The Glasgow clubs presented their cases on Monday and the tribunal will now undertake a period of deliberation before announcing whether the sanctions stand.
The stadium closure penalty was announced in late August following the disorder at the end of last season's quarter-final tie at Ibrox, which Celtic won after a penalty shoot-out.
They clubs are also challenging fines of £100,000 after their fans clashed on the Ibrox pitch.

highlights.title: Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave Actor Based Fabio On an Iconic Disney Villain
highlights.summary: It's been several weeks since the launch of Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and fans around the world are still sinking their teeth into the massive strategy RPG. With a sprawling cast featuring dozens of unique characters, it's no small feat for one to emerge as a clear fan favorite.
body: Yet that's precisely what's happened with Fabio, the condescending scholar of mysterious origins who becomes Dietrich's right-hand man in the Heroic Games tournament. Actor Jimmy Yamaguchi's heartfelt and often hilarious performance has contributed immeasurably to the character's popularity, and he recently revealed the unexpected inspiration for Fabio's voice in an interview with Polygon.

"His accent is actually probably more like a mid-Atlantic accent. Someone who has lived in multiple places. So it's not distinctly anything. One of the inspirations, at first, was Jeremy Irons," Yamaguchi told Polygon. "When I got the specs, before I started reading the lines, I did something like, 'Well, I was first in line... until the little hairball was born.' And then I went into the line as I did it, so that way, I could kind of get an idea."

highlights.title: Self-destructive or helpful? How to harness envy for your benefit
highlights.summary: In her new book, Envy, Stacy Kim explains how to understand the feeling, identify your deeper desires and use them to achieve your goals. In the 16th-century poem The Faerie Queene, envy is a ghoulish figure riding a ravenous wolf, sad to see the fortune of others and “wonderous glad” of their…
body: Maybe not. “I think that when we don’t examine our envy, that’s when it leads us astray,” says Dr Stacy Kim, social scientist, life coach and author of the new book Envy: Why Wanting What They Have is the Key to Getting What You Want. Kim wrote the book after seeing the way envy came up for her coaching clients and reflecting on the role it had in her own life. The book is informed by social science and philosophy research, as well as her personal and professional experiences.

To Kim, a lifelong envier who says sibling rivalry propelled her to fast-track a PhD in educational policy and leadership, envy tells you “there’s something important here,” Kim says. “Envy signals to us our goals,” as well as “what is within our reach”, as we tend to envy people similar to ourselves more so than, say, superstars.
But how to transform envy from sulky to superpower? Kim gave us some points to consider.
Envy is “simply wanting something that someone else has”, Kim says. “Everyone envies – it’s normal.”

highlights.title: Highway thieves are spoofing GPS to steal millions in data center-bound cargo
highlights.summary: Highway thieves are using sophisticated digital tactics that investigators worry make it easy to rob trucks carrying millions in expensive data center equipment. NBC News spoke to “several industry leaders, consultants, and investigators advising law enforcement” offices probing the biggest thefts…
body: Equipment commonly targeted includes “servers, fiber-optic cables, computer memory chips, copper wires, and bitcoin mining machines,” NBC News reported.

Some trailers hit seem to be carrying only data center equipment, like two stolen freights found in Illinois. The Cook County Sheriff’s Office estimated those contained $300,000 worth of copper wire spools and about $1 million in “custom-made data center modular power solutions equipment,” NBC News reported. Other trucks impacted were carrying additional freight, like a Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department case where “data center cooling equipment” bound for Deepcool AI was recovered among nicotine pouches, televisions, shoes, printers, speakers, and skin care cosmetics. Experts worry that means Americans may be broadly harmed by the thefts, not just the AI industry.

While some stolen goods have been recovered, in two of the largest thefts that NBC News found, none of the equipment was found, and off-duty cops hired to escort the shipments were targeted in hit-and-runs.

highlights.title: Can AI help solve the COBOL code crisis?
highlights.summary: What do the IRS, banks, airlines, and government infrastructure around the world have in common? They're all running on systems propped up by antique computer code that nobody dares touch, lest everything come crashing down. OpenAI thinks it may have a solution.
body: The ancient code holding the world together may meet its match in AI. Today is not that day.

OpenAI thinks it may have a solution. On October 19th, the company touted “substantial improvements” in its latest AI models’ ability to migrate aging software written in older programming languages into modern code, which it claims could help organizations with “maintaining and modernizing older systems.”

That’s a potentially massive deal. COBOL, one of the languages highlighted by OpenAI, remains stubbornly embedded in vast portions of the world’s critical infrastructure. And despite decades of efforts to banish it to history, the language has limped on, simply refusing to die.
“Nobody in their right mind would use COBOL for a new development project.”

highlights.title: Interactive Storytelling App OOC Introduces Halloween Event with Special Rewards
highlights.summary: Have you ever been watching an anime and felt like you just wanted to step into that world? Well, OOC: The Playable Anime was created to offer exactly that experience, and right now it’s hosting a Halloween event with special rewards that allow newcomers to experience more stories.
body: For the uninitiated, OOC is interactive storytelling and roleplaying app that lets you become the protagonist and actively participate in how a story unfolds. There’s a preset world with its own lore, characters, and starting point, but where things go from there is based on what you type. You make choices and use custom prompts to shape the story’s twists and turns, and those choices can dramatically alter the characters and story. What if you had the power to determine whether the serial killer in a horror story ultimately wins? You can do that during OOC’s Halloween.

Whatever story and world you choose to dive into, characters remember your previous conversations and decisions, allowing relationships to naturally develop. As the storyline and world are shaped by your choices, scenes become more vivid and immersive thanks to images that reflect how these scenes play out. Every time you experience a story, it’s exclusive to you alone.

Some stories are OOC Originals from the app itself, while others are created by members of the community, which you can do too. There are currently more than 52,000 stories and more than 58,000 characters to interact with.

body: Handling the art side of things was my gallery colleague Brian Ladd and together we landed in a wintery Manhattan in January with about 25 guests largely, shall we say, a certain demographic who were keen to sample the cultural delights of the great metropolis.

And let’s face it, there’s no shortage of them. We took in the Metropolitan Museum and the Cloisters, MoMA, the Frick, the Whitney, Radio City, the Brooklyn Museum, the Guggenheim, the High Line, half a dozen shows and several exhaustive bus tours from one end of the island to the other with our indefatigable local guide Frederique. We even managed a backstage tour of the Met, led by a volunteer who actually paid for the privilege of conducting them! A full-on schedule but, let me tell you, no one goes harder than an active senior in search of cultural enrichment. By the end of the 10 days, we were desperately in need of a holiday.

highlights.title: As Peggy Flanagan Runs for Senate, a Look Back At Her Intentional Style
highlights.summary: Peggy Flanagan could become the first Indigenous woman elected to the U.S. Senate. On the campaign trail, she has been using her platform to spotlight Native designers.
body: During next week’s midterm elections, Peggy Flanagan could make history as the first Indigenous woman elected to the U.S. Senate.

In the tight race to the midterms, Flanagan has been focusing on priorities such as providing affordable healthcare, maintaining climate and agricultural policies, offering better access to reproductive healthcare and abortion, and protecting the rights of local Indigenous communities. Her fashion choices on the campaign trail, however, have been just as intentional: Flanagan has been using her platform to champion Indigenous designers.

A member of the White Earth Band of Ojibwe, Flanagan has been uplifting Indigenous designs—both traditional and contemporary—on a national stage. Back at the 2024 DNC—when Flanagan was working on the Walz-Harris campaign—she wore a black and white Parfleche blazer and skirt by Jamie Okuma, one of the most prominent Indigenous designers, and the only one to be inducted into the CFDA. Flanagan accessorized the look with a pair of Copper Canoe Woman statement earrings, another contemporary Native label. “I really want those earrings,” one viewer noted, while another simply exclaimed, “She is fabulous!”

highlights.title: Five weird details from Anthropic’s IPO filing
highlights.summary: Anthropic has finally filed its S-1 prospectus with the SEC, a document designed to give investors a look under the hood of its business, from how much its executives are making and plans for spending its IPO billions to the risks that could derail its ambitions.
body: From conscious AI and ‘catastrophic’ risk to unusual corporate structures and executive perks.

Sibling co-founders Dario Amodei and Daniela Amodei are the two most highly-paid executives at Anthropic, according to the filing. Last year, CEO Dario’s compensation totaled nearly $18 million, most of which came from stock and option awards. President Daniela, meanwhile, received $16.4 million. Admittedly, it is at the lower end of the Big Tech scale, but it is still a tidy sum.

And that’s not all. Anthropic also spent $2.75 million on “personal security services” for Dario and $1.29 million for “personal protection, home security, and transportation services” for Daniela. Dario also gets access to a private jet for personal use, which cost the company another $97,055.
The company says its success is “highly dependent on the continued service” of its senior team, particularly Dario and Daniela, who “are critical” to advancing the company’s research and mission.

highlights.title: Meet the AI Agents Trying to Be Real-Life Journalists

body: Would-be football journalist Jayden isn’t having much luck placing stories these days. “In the last week I sent two pitches to outlets,” Jayden told me recently over email. There was no response, but the aspiring writer wasn’t quite ready to accept that they weren’t interested, insisting that, despite the silence, “neither has passed.” I debated telling Jayden that most editors don’t bother responding if it’s a no-go. Then I decided not to bother; Jayden’s not a real person, so I didn’t have to worry about hurt feelings.
Jayden is both a wannabe reporter and a bot. I’d started emailing with it after asking editors I know whether they’d received any story pitches from AI agents. The answer was a resounding yes.

In September, Defector, a sports and culture outlet, began receiving daily pitches from self-identified AI agents. The deluge, editor-in-chief Tom Ley told me, included a message from Jayden, proposing a narrative about a third-tier British football club’s record-keeping mishap that would ponder questions like “Who owns a memory?”

highlights.summary: The last few months at Xbox Studios have been a bloodbath. Microsoft announced in July that it would be cutting 3,200 jobs from its Xbox division in the coming year and has since made over 1,800 cuts. As part of those layoffs, Xbox also announced it would cut several beloved game studios.
body: Beyond Ninja Theory, Dishonored developer Arkane Lyon seems to be the last major studio that Microsoft is considering closing as part of its ongoing “reset.” Arkane Lyon is based in France, which has stronger labor laws than the U.S. and many other countries, so Xbox must undergo a consultation process to “review potential strategic options” about what to do with the studio.

As per PC Gamer, French outlet Le Monde previously reported that while Xbox intended to shut down Arkane, France’s “Florange Law” requires companies with more than 1,000 employees to seek potential buyers first. Originally, the deadline for Arkane to find a buyer was Nov. 13, 2026, after which Microsoft would seemingly be free to close the studio. Several months into the consultation process, Arkane still does not appear to have found a buyer.

highlights.title: Sharjah Film Festival Partners With UAE’s Media Authority in Push to Assist Emerging Filmmakers
highlights.summary: The Sharjah Intl. Film Festival for Children and Youth is adding a federal partner to its push to build a more substantial and sustainable pipeline for emerging filmmakers.
body: The partnership comes as SIFF increasingly looks beyond screenings and workshops to the practical hurdles facing young filmmakers trying to enter the industry. Ahead of the festival, SIFF director Sheikha Jawaher bint Abdullah Al Qasimi told Variety that learning to make a film represents only one part of that journey.

“Our agreement with the National Media Authority reflects this commitment,” Al Qasimi said Monday. “It is an important step in bringing together national efforts to support the film industry and help emerging filmmakers turn their ideas and perspectives into creative work.”

The new agreement addresses another piece of that infrastructure. The National Media Authority will help facilitate permits required to screen participating films, coordinating, where necessary, with embassies, consulates, cultural organizations and government entities. Festival teams will also receive training on the authority’s electronic services and technical support intended to streamline regulatory procedures.
